assessments.guidance: Dataverse sandbox plug-ins must target the .NET Framework version the platform supports. If the project targets something else, that is the project's reality: record it and do not retarget existing assemblies as part of adopting the harness.

assessments.standardLabel: SDK-style projects, deployed as Dataverse .nupkg plug-in packages
assessments.guidance: Legacy non-SDK csproj files still build. Converting them is a migration with its own risk, not a side effect of installing standards.
A signed assembly already registered in Dataverse cannot be unsigned without re-registering every step. If the project signs, the standard has to follow the project.
A project on NUnit or MSTest, or on a different xUnit version, keeps it. Two test frameworks in one repository is worse than an out-of-date standard.
FakeXrmEasy 2.x requires a licence key at runtime; 1.x does not. A project on 1.x is a deliberate choice, not an oversight.

assessments.detail: The package is optional and is not referenced.
assessments.guidance: Only relevant where the repository already simulates messages or Custom APIs in tests.

assessments.standardLabel: React virtual controls (control-type="virtual") with platform libraries
assessments.detail: No PCF controls in the repository.
assessments.guidance: Standard controls that bundle their own React work today. Migrating them to virtual is a change with import-time risk; it does not belong in a scaffolding step.

assessments.detail: No PCF controls in the repository.
assessments.guidance: The version in ControlManifest.Input.xml is what the environment actually loads. The standard must state the version the repository ships, never a newer one.

assessments.detail: No PCF controls in the repository.
assessments.guidance: A Fluent platform-library version higher than the one the target environment supports fails solution import. Record the repository's version, not the standard's.

assessments.detail: No relevant JavaScript or PCF code with a package.json.
assessments.guidance: A repository already on Jest keeps Jest. Running both runners in one repository doubles the configuration surface for no gain.

assessments.standardLabel: Plain ES2020 JavaScript, no build or bundling step
assessments.detail: Web resources are authored in TypeScript, so the committed file is not the deployed file.
assessments.guidance: Web resources authored in TypeScript, or bundled, contradict this rule end to end: the file committed is no longer the file deployed. Decide which one the project follows before the first change, not during it.
Same rule as PCF: one runner per repository. A project that runs its web resource tests under jsdom keeps it: the environment is a per-project choice, not a defect.

ESLint 8 with .eslintrc, or ESLint 9, is not a defect. ESLint 9 reached end of life on 2026-08-06; moving to 10 enables three more recommended rules and is its own task, as is migrating to flat config.

assessments.standardLabel: SDK-style .esproj project (Microsoft.VisualStudio.JavaScript.Sdk/1.0.6887863, version pinned) with Vitest + ESLint tooling, under src/PowerPlatform/WebResources/<ProjectName>.WebResources/
assessments.detail: Web resources have test/lint tooling but no SDK-style project file.
assessments.guidance: A repository that already edits web resources without this project is not broken. Never retrofit an existing, differently structured WebResources setup: offer this during reconciliation instead of writing it silently. An existing .esproj that pins a different SDK version keeps its version; only an .esproj with no version at all fails to load and needs one.

assessments.standard: src/PowerPlatform/{Plugins,CustomAPIs,WebResources} in src/PowerPlatform/PowerPlatform.sln, one project per table or Custom API with its .Tests project beside it, docs/adr
assessments.standardLabel: The folder layout the standards reference by path: src/PowerPlatform/ with PowerPlatform.sln, a shared <ProjectName>.Common project, and each plugin or Custom API project next to its test project
assessments.detail: Missing from the expected layout: src/PowerPlatform/Plugins, src/PowerPlatform/CustomAPIs, src/PowerPlatform/WebResources, docs/adr
assessments.guidance: Creating this layout next to a different existing one leaves two conventions in one repository. In an existing project, create only what is missing and only where it matches what is already there.

ProjectName.source: First segment of the existing root namespace (Acme.Crm)

PublisherUniqueName.source: Not derivable: no committed solution manifest and no exported solution

PublisherPrefix.source: Not derivable: no committed solution manifest and no exported solution

CoreSolution.source: No committed solution and no environment solution list. Ask for the core solution unique name, or 'none'.

ProjectDescription.source: Ask the user: one or two sentences on what the project delivers

warnings: The existing C# projects use the root namespace Acme.Crm, but the harness uses the project name as the root namespace and a project name cannot contain dots. The generated docs will say Acme.<Entity> and Acme.Common: reconcile them to Acme.Crm after scaffolding.
The harness is partially installed. Only the missing files will be written; compare the present ones against the templates before assuming they are current.
